metadata.title: Odin OS: Cryptographically Authorized Memory Mutation in a RISC-V PMP-Enforced Agent Execution Environment
metadata.description:
Odin OS (Phase B.3 Publication Candidate) is a bare-metal, zero-allocation (#![no_std]) 64-bit RISC-V microkernel that anchors autonomous AI agent capability boundaries directly into processor Physical Memory Protection (PMP) hardware comparators. Operating on the central axiom that state that cannot prove its right to exist cannot be committed to memory or disk, Odin OS enforces capability containment via cache-line aligned 256-byte binary tokens termed TransitionDeeds.

This publication release establishes: (1) zero-allocation RFC 8032 Ed25519 digital signature verification in pure #![no_std] against a pinned 32-byte root public key; (2) complete bi-directional W^X hardware memory protection; (3) dynamic capability lease revocation (SYS_REVOKE_LEASE); (4) a deterministic 17-case adversarial matrix with 100% hardware enforcement; (5) machine-checked formal SMT verification via Z3 5.3.1 proving integer overflow immunity, memory disjointness, and anti-replay monotonicity; (6) 100% mutation testing sensitivity (15/15 killed); and (7) end-to-end coupling with local neural inference on google/gemma-4-e4b.
